bad.title: No, to what?
bad.text: With the question blurred, No could mean don’t delete or don’t keep.

bad.title: Yes looks like the safe next step
bad.text: It’s the filled button, and it erases the email.

good.title: Keep draft makes sense alone
good.text: People who read only the buttons still know this one saves the email.

good.title: Delete draft names the loss
good.text: A verb and an object say what goes before anyone presses it.

bad.title: Execute query, not search
bad.text: It names what the database does. People looking for Maria have to translate it.

bad.title: Instantiate contact means nothing to most
bad.text: Some people won’t risk a button they can’t read, so they never add anyone.

good.title: Search, the word people think in
good.text: It matches the task, find Maria, so nobody stops to work it out.

good.title: Add contact says what happens
good.text: The same words people use for their own address book.

bad.title: Add To Cart in Title Case
bad.text: Right next to Save for later, it looks like it came from another app.

bad.title: Two links, two styles
bad.text: Size Guide sits beside Shipping and returns, and the mismatch shows first.

bad.title: The heading picks a third look
bad.text: Customers Also Bought adds one more capital pattern to a small screen.

good.title: Add to cart matches its neighbor
good.text: Both buttons follow one style, so people read the words, not the capitals.

good.title: Both links in sentence case
good.text: Size guide and Shipping and returns read as one row.

good.title: The heading follows the same rule
good.text: Customers also bought matches every button and link above it.

bad.title: Remove sounds mild
bad.text: People expect the photo to leave the album and stay in their library.
bad.wait: Open the photo’s menu to see this.

bad.title: Then the dialog says Delete
bad.text: It erases from the library and every device. Is that what Remove meant?
bad.wait: Press Remove in the photo’s menu to see this.

good.title: Remove from album says from where
good.text: The menu item names what the photo leaves, so the library isn’t in question.
good.wait: Open the photo’s menu to see this.

good.title: The dialog repeats Remove
good.text: Same verb as the menu, so people confirm what they meant to do.
good.wait: Press Remove from album in the photo’s menu to see this.

bad.title: Blames the person, hides the rule
bad.text: Invalid how? People still have to guess that the limit is 99.
bad.wait: Type 150 in Quantity and press Update to see this.

good.title: The rule, in neutral words
good.text: From 1 to 99 tells people exactly what to type, so one try fixes it.
good.wait: Type 150 in Quantity and press Update to see this.

bad.title: Error 552 5.3.4, nothing else
bad.text: Is it the file, the app or the network? A screen reader spells it out digit by digit.

bad.title: 38 MB, the real cause
bad.text: The size is right there, but nothing links it to the error.

good.title: Not sent, and why
good.text: 38 MB against a 25 MB limit. People know to shrink the file.

good.title: 38 MB, now explained
good.text: The message names this number, so people see what to change.

good.title: The code waits behind Show details
good.text: Support can still ask for it, and nobody else has to read it.

bad.title: OK is the only way out
bad.text: It closes the message and leaves Sam without access. The fix is somewhere else.
bad.wait: Press Send to Sam to see this.

bad.title: The fix hides in Sharing settings
bad.text: Give access, Back, then Send again. Six clicks in all.

good.title: Give Sam access, right there
good.text: One press grants access and sends the link.
good.wait: Press Send to Sam to see this.

good.title: Sharing settings isn’t needed
good.text: The message does the job, so the whole task takes two clicks.

bad.title: FATAL ERROR for a dropped connection
bad.text: In red capitals, DATA MAY BE LOST makes people think the packing list is gone.
bad.wait: Turn Wi-Fi off to see this.

bad.title: The note is still there
bad.text: Nothing was lost, but the message never says so.

good.title: Offline, said calmly
good.text: It says what happened and what still works: saved on this device.
good.wait: Turn Wi-Fi off to see this.

good.title: People keep typing
good.text: The banner says the note syncs later, so there’s no reason to stop.

bad.title: Utilize, initiate, input
bad.text: Three words that slow people down, then RMA and SKU with no explanation.

bad.title: RMA, but the email says return number
bad.text: People have to guess that R-4417 belongs here.

good.title: Use, start, enter
good.text: Everyday verbs people read without slowing down.

good.title: Return number, and where to find it
good.text: The label matches the email, and the hint points people to it.

bad.title: The preview ends before the point
bad.text: Maintenance, then ongoing work. What stops working, and when, is cut off.

good.title: What and when, then why
good.text: Payments, transfers and Sunday 1 to 5 am fit in the preview. The reason comes last.

bad.title: Five ideas in one breath
bad.text: The 5 days sit between the pickup code and the 3 extra days, easy to mix up.

bad.title: 52 words before the first period
bad.text: People reread it, and some add the extension and pick 8 days.

good.title: One fact per sentence
good.text: You have 5 days gets its own sentence, so people find it on the first read.

good.title: No sentence over 10 words
good.text: Short enough to hold in mind while answering the question.

bad.title: Bag in the header
bad.text: The first name people see for the place their items go.

bad.title: Add to basket on the button
bad.text: A second word. Is the basket the same as the bag?

bad.title: Then Added to cart
bad.text: A third name, so people wonder where the scarf really went.
bad.wait: Press Add to basket to see this.

good.title: Cart in the header
good.text: The place gets one name, and people learn it once.

good.title: Add to cart, the same word
good.text: The button points at the place people can already see.

good.title: Added to cart confirms it
good.text: The message repeats the word, so the count going up in Cart makes sense.
good.wait: Press Add to cart to see this.
